extracted.intended_audience: authors of randomised controlled trials; clinical researchers; journal editors and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance/checklist items for complete, transparent reporting of randomized (controlled) trials to ensure reproducibility and correct interpretation by readers and reviewers. Covers title/abstract, introduction, full methods, results, discussion, and administrative information (registration, protocol, funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification as a randomised trial in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear in the title that the study is a randomized trial (e.g., 'randomised', 'randomized', 'randomised controlled trial') so that readers and indexers can identify study design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured summary of trial design, methods, results, and conclusions (for specific guidance see CONSORT for abstracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a structured abstract format that includes background, objectives, trial design, participants, interventions, primary outcomes, results (with effect sizes and precision), conclusions, trial registration and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific background and explanation of rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the trial was done, the problem addressed, and the existing evidence base that justifies the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives or hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific objectives or hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State primary and key secondary objectives or pre-specified hypotheses clearly and, if applicable, the estimand of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial design
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of trial design (such as parallel, factorial), including allocation ratio. Important changes to methods after trial commencement (such as eligibility criteria), with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the type of design, how groups are compared, allocation ratio, and document any protocol or methodological changes with rationale and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility criteria for participants and the settings and locations where the data were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define inclusion and exclusion criteria, recruitment settings (primary/secondary care, community), and geographic/temporal context; report screening and recruitment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The interventions for each group with sufficient details to allow replication, including how and when they were actually administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intervention components, dose, schedule, delivery personnel, fidelity/adherence strategies, and any comparator (placebo, usual care) details necessary for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes — pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Completely defined pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures, including how and when they were assessed. Important changes to outcomes after trial commencement, with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define outcome variables, measurement instruments, timing, units, and clinical relevance; report any outcome modifications and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: How sample size was determined. When applicable, explanation of any interim analyses and stopping guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the assumptions used (effect size, alpha, power, variance), the target sample size, and details of any planned interim analyses or stopping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation — sequence generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Method used to generate the random allocation sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the randomisation method (e.g., computer-generated random numbers, block sizes, stratification factors) and any restrictions applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation — allocation concealment mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism used to implement the random allocation sequence (such as sequentially numbered containers), describing any steps taken to conceal the sequence until interventions were assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how allocation was concealed (central randomisation, opaque sealed envelopes), who was responsible for concealment, and how implementation protected against foreknowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation — implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Who generated the random allocation sequence, who enrolled participants, and who assigned participants to interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify roles (sequence generator, enrolment, assignment) to assess risk of selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (masking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether participants, care providers, and outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment; if relevant, describe how the success of blinding was assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State who was blinded, how blinding was maintained, and consequences if blinding was not possible; describe objective measures to reduce bias where blinding impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes, including any methods for additional analyses (e.g. subgroup analyses, adjusted analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify primary analysis population (intention-to-treat, per-protocol), models/tests used, handling of multiplicity, covariate adjustment, and methods for missing data (imputation methods if used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant flow (diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, numbers of participants who were randomised, received intended treatment, and were analysed for the primary outcome. Losses and exclusions after randomisation, with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a flow diagram showing enrolment, allocation, follow-up and analysis numbers and reasons for exclusions/dropouts to permit assessment of attrition bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow‑up, and why the trial ended or was stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recruitment start/stop dates, follow-up duration, status at pre-specified endpoints, and reasons for early stopping if applicable (with reference to interim analyses or external factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline data
rubrics_metrics.description: A table showing baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present key prognostic variables and important covariates for comparability across groups; avoid over-interpretation of baseline imbalances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers analysed
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, number of participants (denominator) included in each analysis and whether the analysis was by original assigned groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State denominators for analyses, clarify if analyses followed intention-to-treat, per-protocol or other populations, and report reasons for exclusions from analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each primary and secondary outcome, results for each group, estimated effect size and its precision (such as 95% confidence interval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute and relative effect sizes where appropriate, along with confidence intervals and exact p-values; present both unadjusted and adjusted estimates if reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of any other analyses performed, including subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses, distinguishing pre‑specified from exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label which analyses were pre-specified and which were exploratory; provide rationale and avoid overemphasis of post hoc findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms (adverse events)
rubrics_metrics.description: All important harms or unintended effects in each group (for specific guidance see CONSORT for harms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the nature, frequency, severity, and relatedness of adverse events by group; describe methods for collecting and adjudicating harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial limitations, addressing sources of potential bias, imprecision, and, if relevant, multiplicity of analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss limitations candidly (selection bias, performance bias, detection bias, attrition, small sample size, generalizability issues) and their likely direction and magnitude of effect on results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (external validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalisability of the trial findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider to which populations, settings, and care-contexts the results apply; discuss differences between trial conditions and routine practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation consistent with results, balancing benefits and harms, and considering other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide balanced conclusions that reflect the strength and precision of the evidence, noting clinical relevance and implications for practice/research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration, protocol, and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration number and name of trial registry. Where the full trial protocol can be accessed. Sources of funding and other support, role of funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registry identifier, link to full protocol and statistical analysis plan, describe sponsor/funder involvement in design, conduct, analysis, and reporting, and disclose conflicts of interest.
